Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Compiled scripts start from the screen the script before leaves**: a compiled script that carries on from another one's screen (a character still standing there, the stage, the music) now has it in its saved states, so going back, loading and thumbnails there show it. A script that scripts with different screens go to (a menu every chapter returns to) starts from an empty World, as before
- **Going back to the middle of a message window draws the window as it was**: BACK, a backlog mark or a load at a line that carries on a window draws its earlier lines first, instead of the line alone
- **kagex-release keeps `.psd` and `.clip` files** by default: *Leave out* is `*.bak`, `*.tmp`, `Thumbs.db`, `desktop.ini` and `.DS_Store` now. A `release.json` with 0.9.2's default list gets the new one
- kagex-release 0.9.3 downloads the 0.9.3 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.9.3/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tool aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tool, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
